caption:
Google is reportedly developing a custom chip — codenamed "Frozen v2" — that bakes Gemini's model architecture directly into the silicon.

Instead of running the AI on general-purpose accelerators, hard-wiring its structure into the hardware could reportedly make it 6 to 10× more efficient at Gemini workloads.

If it ships, it could sharply cut the cost and energy of serving AI at Google's scale — and squeeze rivals still leaning on off-the-shelf GPUs.

Would a model-specific chip give Google a real edge, or lock it into today's architecture? 👇
